page.layout: Full-width running head at top, with page number at top left. Below it, two circular medallion portraits side by side, each with a legend around its rim (left: Darius; right: Zopyrus). Below them, one column of running text in two paragraphs, the second beginning with the name ZOPYRVS. No marginal notes, no catchword, no signature.

main_text.l: DARIVS HIST[?]ASPIS FIL. REX PERS. IIII
SOPIRVS NOB. PER.
DARIVS Hystaspis filius, hinnitu equi rex declaratus est
anno mundi 3441. ante Christum natum 521. Smerdis & Pa-
tizithes qui regnum usurparant, occisi sunt antequam impera-
ret hic, qui etiam Smerdin occidit, detecta per Otanem eius
fraude: nam Smerdis hic, se Cambysis fratrem dicebat, quòd
illi de facie ac nomine similis esset: attamen ab aurium muti-
latione dolus deprehensus est. Porrò Darius hic, Atossam Cyri
filiam uxorem duxit, ex qua liberos sustulit, inter quos Xerxes
fuit: hanc atossam putant nonnulli fuisse Hester. hic permisit
Judæis remigrare in Judæam ac templum reædificare: vasa &
thesauros templi restituit. Provincias viginti constituit,
earúmque singulis præsides præfecit, taxato quod penderetur
tributo. etenim sub Cyro & Cambyse nihil dum fuerat circa
tributa institutum, sed munera afferebatur. hic Geras subegit,
Thraces se dedidere: at Scythæ hunc in fugam adegêre. Vide
Herod.lib.3. nam Justit.lib.1. Smerdin, sive Smerdem, de quo
supra, Oropastem vocat.
ZOPYRVS, præcisis de industria, labiis, naso, auribus,
nomine tranfugæ Babylonem profectus, corpus populo lania-
tum ostendit: constituitur dux omnium suffragio adversus
Darium, qui Babylonem iandiu frustra obsidebat, cui tandem
creditum sibi exercitum prodidit: sicque Babylonem quæ de-
fecerat, & ab Assyriis occupabatur, recuperavit Darius, memo-
rabili hoc quidem facto Zopyri: cui fuit etiam Megabizus fi-
lius, dux exercitus Darij in Europa, qui & Thraciam subegit.
Herod.lib.3.Justit.lib.1.

page.notes: Medallion legends are printed in a circle around the portraits; the left legend's middle word is partly obscured, hence [?]. Printed page number "110" is set in small old-style figures and is uncertain. The left legend's first word may read differently. Running head has u/v normalised per rule 5 (PROMPTV. ICONVM printed).
